stem: A reviewer at Ashgrove Media runs `terraform plan -target aws_instance.example` against a configuration where that instance's own arguments reference a separate security group resource. What does the resulting plan actually cover?

choices.text: Only aws_instance.example itself, with the security group left out of the plan entirely
Every resource in the configuration, the same as an untargeted plan would cover
Nothing at all — this kind of single-resource target selection is only accepted by destroy, never by plan
aws_instance.example and the security group it references

rationale: -target extends the selection to include whatever the targeted resource itself depends on, so the security group the instance references is pulled into the same plan. Leaving the security group out entirely ignores that extension. -target narrows the plan; it does not fall back to covering everything. -target is accepted by plan, which this lesson covers alongside its use with destroy, so refusing to run is not what happens.
